title: Question 3: Economic Development ($100 million)

context.text: Placed on the ballot by the General Assembly: the Rhode Island Voter Information Handbook describes Questions 1 through 5 as authorizing the State to borrow through bonds and temporary notes for capital investments under an act passed at the January 2026 session (Chapter 084, Public Laws 2026).

question.text: Shall the act passed by the General Assembly at the January 2026 session, allowing the State of Rhode Island to issue bonds, refunding bonds, and temporary notes to pay for the projects listed below, be approved, and the State be allowed to issue these bonds, refunding bonds, and temporary notes as outlined in the law? 3. ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT - $100,000,000 To fund site development and growth industry infrastructure for economic development purposes, to be allocated as follows: a. Site Development - $55,000,000 b. Growth Industry Infrastructure - $45,000,000

summary.text: The bond would provide $100,000,000: $55,000,000 for site development (land acquisition or assembly, environmental remediation, infrastructure and utility installation and site preparation, including industrial sites, the Quonset Business Park and the I-195 District) and $45,000,000 for growth-industry infrastructure for Rhode Island's ocean, defense, life sciences and data analytics/cybersecurity industries. Official cost estimate in the handbook (assuming 5% interest and level payments over 20 years): principal $100,000,000, interest $60,483,750, total $160,483,750.

measure.yesMeans: A vote to Approve means that you support the State issuing $100,000,000 in general obligation bonds for economic development purposes.
measure.noMeans: A vote to Reject means that you are against the State issuing $100,000,000 in general obligation bonds for economic development purposes.

sources.title: A Guide to State Referenda and Voting Procedures in Rhode Island: General Election November 3, 2026 (Voter Information Handbook)

researchNotes: The ballot text, approve/reject statements and cost estimates are from the Rhode Island Department of State's 2026 Voter Information Handbook (PDF text extracted and checked by script). The handbook publishes no arguments for or against, and no registered campaign statements or news quotations for either side were found, so neither argument list is filled. The Secretary of State's website and Ballotpedia blocked automated requests; the five-question list is from the handbook, which covers all statewide referenda.
